label: early original-phase input of 3/f/e/c/d/x (steps 1-3)
explanation: Fires almost only in the original (input) phase (99.9% of mass), with no activity at <DEL> and almost none during copy. It is concentrated at steps 1-3 (about 90% of mass) and dies out by step 5-6. Token selectivity: the digit 3 (rate 31%) and the letters f, e, c, d, x (16-21%) are strongly preferred; s, z, 1, v are weaker, and b and u rarely fire. The strongest activations come at steps 2-3 when one of these tokens follows an early prefix such as a o / a a / r o, and often when the preferred tokens come back-to-back (e.g. a o f 3 e). It is not a first-occurrence detector: repeats like 3 3 activate strongly. Magnitude is graded by position and context, which a step+token predicate cannot fully capture. Recall misses weaker activations on other tokens, and precision falls off at later steps (4+), where these same tokens often do not fire. Dev F1 is about 0.66, mass recall 0.76.
